original_client_text.markup_text:
The Insane Engineering Behind DeepSeek Harness

DeepSeek Harness launched on August 13, 2026, and within 48 hours had picked up nearly four times its opening-day GitHub stars, a pace DeepSeek's own AI models never came close to matching. The reason has almost nothing to do with the model it runs on. DeepSeek Harness is built entirely out of interchangeable plugins (everything is a plugin), letting developers swap the AI model, the toolset, or the interface without touching the underlying code. An approach most AI coding agents avoid because it's notoriously hard to get right. This video breaks down the engineering that makes it work, including Cordis, the plugin framework underneath it that turns out to have a longer and more interesting history than the launch coverage let on.

At the center of it is a deceptively simple problem: how do you let a system rebuild itself out of removable parts without it slowly falling apart from leftover, half-removed pieces? The answer involves two mechanisms working together: one that gives every action its own built-in undo instruction, and one that lets components adapt automatically when what they depend on changes. Whether this architecture becomes the standard other AI agent harnesses get compared against, or gets overtaken by something built the same way, is still very much an open question.

aweme_info.content_desc: ["DeepSeek Just Ordered 160,000 HUAWEI AI Chips #news #technology #china #ai ","","DeepSeek is lining up more than one hundred sixty thousand Huawei Ascend nine five zero DT chips for a single data center in Inner Mongolia, and if it lands, it becomes the largest Huawei AI chip cluster ever built. The Ascend nine five zero DT is Huawei's newest AI accelerator, packed with one hundred forty four gigabytes of high bandwidth memory and four terabytes per second of data speed, built to run already trained AI models at massive scale rather than train them from scratch. DeepSeek still trains its models on Nvidia hardware, which is the twist nobody expected from a company betting this big on domestic chips. Inner Mongolia was picked for cheap power and a cold climate that keeps server racks running nonstop, part of China's broader push to move computing power west. But the real story is production. Huawei is expected to make only a few hundred thousand of these chips this year, meaning this single order alone could take over a year to fill. DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng has said four Huawei chips together roughly match one Nvidia card in performance, and that the hardware and software are ready, the only real bottleneck is manufacturing capacity. This is a live look at China's race to build AI infrastructure independent of American chips, one massive order at a time. Watch to see how close China's chip industry actually is to catching up, and where the gap still remains wide open."]

DeepSeek just released a new AI harness, and it may change how we think about what actually makes an AI agent good.

The model is only half the system.

The harness is everything around it: tools, sessions, sandboxes, subagents, loops, storage, and the structure that lets intelligence actually get work done.

DeepSeek’s version is built around Cordis and an idea called spatiotemporal composability, which makes much of that architecture unusually modular.

And recent research found that improving the harness alone, while keeping the underlying model frozen, boosted Terminal-Bench 2 performance from 69.7% to 77%.

So the next AI breakthrough might not be a smarter brain.

It might be a better harness.
